rationale: Confirmed mathematical falsehood in c2 and step i1's predict.reveal: both claim reading k off the wrong exponent (a's power instead of b's) is only 'forgiven' by coincidence for small n and 'will not' be forgiven for larger n, illustrated by 'In (a+b)^8 the same slip would give 70 instead of 56.' This is impossible: C(n,k)=C(n,n-k) is an unconditional identity (the very fact this course proves correct elsewhere, e.g. bt-01-03/k3, BtSymmetryAndSum, BtEntryIsChoose), so swapping which exponent supplies k ALWAYS returns the identical coefficient for every n, not sometimes. Step k2's commonErrors entry for value 70 compounds this: it labels 70 as arising from 'k was read off the power of a' for the term a^5 b^3, but k=5 (a's power) gives C(8,5)=56 (the correct answer, matching by the same identity), not 70 -- the stated misconception mechanism cannot produce the value it is attached to. The graded numeric answer itself (56) is correct and C(7,3)=35, C(7,4)=35, C(8,3)=56 all check out; the defect is confined to the false 'symmetry sometimes fails' narrative and the mismatched commonError explanation for 70.
